findings.comment: No Austin Energy approval letter or stamped electrical site plan with Austin Energy approval has been obtained. Submit the proposed Preliminary Electrical Design Plan to Austin Energy for formal review and approval per LDC § 25-4-200, and provide the signed approval letter and stamped electrical site plan with final application submission.
findings.observation: The site is located in Austin, TX (3759 Valley View Road, Austin TX 78704) within Austin Energy's service territory, as confirmed by the presence of Austin Energy Electric Notes and Electric Transmission Notes on Sheet 3 and the identification of Austin Energy as the electrical service provider in the Master Comment Report (Rosemary Avila, Austin Energy). Sheet 21 shows a proposed electrical design with transformers, meters, and underground service lines. The Master Comment Report indicates Austin Energy conducted a design review through Rosemary Avila with reference to a Bluebeam review link. However, no formal Austin Energy approval letter is present in the supplementary documents (Project Review Form, Completeness Check Results, Consolidated Site Plan Application, Master Comment Report, or Engineer's Summary Letter reviewed). No stamped electrical site plan with Austin Energy approval seal or signature is visible. The site is within 200 feet of Austin Energy components per the transmission easement notation, triggering the approval requirement.
findings.reasoning: EL-19.15 specifies 'Approval of electric system plans from Austin Energy not obtained' and applies to 'All sites requiring connection to Austin Energy system or within 200 feet of existing Austin Energy components.' The grouping instruction states to 'Check: Austin Energy approval letter, stamped electrical site plan, ESPA approval documentation.' LDC § 25-4-200 requires that 'All electric system plans for subdivisions and sites requiring connection to Austin Energy's system must obtain approval from Austin Energy.' While the Master Comment Report documents that Austin Energy conducted a review (with comments on Bluebeam), this does not constitute formal approval. No approval letter, stamped plan, or ESPA approval documentation appears in the accessible supplementary documents. The electrical site plan is marked as preliminary, and formal Austin Energy approval is required before the design can be finalized.

findings.comment: Approval of electric system plans from Austin Energy has not been obtained. Site plan is labeled 'Preliminary Electrical Design Plan' and is in first-round comment response phase. An approved/stamped electrical site plan with documented Austin Energy approval letter must be submitted prior to site plan approval, demonstrating compliance with the Austin Energy Design Criteria Manual (UCM Section 1).
findings.observation: The site plan submittal is at the first-round comment response phase (SP-2025-0126C submitted 05/20/2025). The Master Comment Report (p. 2-3) indicates Austin Energy has provided preliminary design requirements through a Bluebeam markup link and lists multiple UCM sections that must be addressed (UCM § 1.3.8, 1.3.12, 1.3.16, 1.9.3, 1.10.3, 1.10.4, 1.10.10.3 & 4). However, no signed Austin Energy approval letter, stamped electrical site plan, or formal approval documentation is visible in the supplementary documents reviewed. Sheet 1 (Cover) shows empty approval stamp boxes with no Austin Energy approval date recorded. The electrical site plan (Sheet 21) is labeled as 'Preliminary Electrical Design Plan' with no indication of Austin Energy Design sign-off. The site is within Austin jurisdiction, has electrical service shown (transformers, meters, underground lines), and is clearly within 200 feet of existing Austin Energy components per the electrical infrastructure layout shown on Sheet 21.
findings.reasoning: LDC § 25-4-200 requires that all electric system plans for subdivisions and sites requiring connection to Austin Energy's system must obtain approval from Austin Energy prior to site plan approval. The grouping narrative states that Austin Energy approval demonstrates compliance with the Austin Energy Design Criteria Manual, which is adopted as part of the Utilities Criteria Manual. Evidence of preliminary design comments from Austin Energy exists (Master Comment Report references Bluebeam markup), but no formal approval letter or stamped approval documentation is visible. The site plan status indicates it is still awaiting first-round comment response, which means Austin Energy approval has not yet been obtained. The site clearly requires Austin Energy service (electrical infrastructure is shown throughout the site plan) and falls within the mandatory approval trigger (within 200 feet of existing Austin Energy components, in fact showing new customer connections). Without documented Austin Energy approval, the requirement for LDC § 25-4-200 is not met.

findings.comment: Obtain and submit a stamped Austin Energy approval letter for the electrical site plan and the Electric Service Planning Application (ESPA) approval per LDC § 25-4-200. The approval must address the proposed electric system design and confirm compliance with Austin Energy Design Criteria Manual (UCM Section 1).
findings.observation: Sheet 21 is labeled 'Preliminary Electrical Design Plan' (emphasis on preliminary). The Master Comment Report confirms 'AE completeness check complete' from Victor Givens (Austin Energy), indicating completeness review has occurred. However, no stamped Austin Energy approval letter is provided in the submitted documentation. The Master Comment Report's Electric Review section references a Bluebeam link for Austin Energy comments (https://studio.bluebeam.com/share/epcafnizivuefw), but the actual Austin Energy approval letter and stamped electrical site plan required by LDC § 25-4-200 are not included in the submitted supplementary documents. The grouping specifically requires 'Austin Energy approval letter, stamped electrical site plan, ESPA approval documentation' to establish compliance.
findings.reasoning: LDC § 25-4-200 requires that 'all electric system plans for subdivisions and sites requiring connection to Austin Energy's system must obtain approval from Austin Energy.' The statute mandates approval, not merely preliminary review. The submission of a 'Preliminary' electrical design plan without an accompanying Austin Energy approval letter does not satisfy this requirement. The completeness check confirmation indicates that Austin Energy has reviewed the plans for completeness (procedural conformance), but approval (substantive compliance with design standards) is a separate and more rigorous determination. Without the formal approval letter and stamped site plan, this requirement is not satisfied.

findings.comment: Proximity survey not provided. If Austin Energy Design has requested a proximity survey showing distances between proposed facilities and existing AE primary voltage facilities, provide the survey documentation.
applicableAreas: areas with existing or proposed AE primary voltage facilities
findings.observation: No survey showing proximities of customer's existing and/or proposed facilities to existing AE primary voltage facilities was located in the supplementary documents. The Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21) shows proposed electrical infrastructure but does not include proximity dimensions to existing AE primary voltage lines. No proximity survey document was found in the project files.
findings.reasoning: When AE Design requests a proximity survey (which is determined during the design coordination process), a survey must be provided showing distances from the customer's facilities to existing AE primary voltage facilities per UCM § 1.10.3. This is typically required when development is within or near AE clearance zones. Without evidence of AE Design requesting this survey, or documentation providing it, the requirement status is unclear. The applicability depends on whether AE Design specifically requested a proximity survey.

findings.comment: Survey not provided showing proximities of customer's existing and/or proposed facilities to existing AE primary voltage facilities as may be required by AE Design. If requested by AE, submit professional survey documenting clearances between proposed buildings, utilities, and equipment from all AE primary voltage transmission facilities.
findings.observation: Master Comment Report indicates Electric Review is complete and preliminary design requirements were provided. Sheet 21 shows electrical design layout but no survey demonstrating proximities of customer's existing and/or proposed facilities to existing AE primary voltage facilities. No proximity survey document located in supplementary documents. Facts.md indicates transmission easements exist, and Sheet 3 transmission notes document 20-25 foot clearance requirements from transmission structures, but no formal survey proving compliance with these clearances is submitted.
findings.reasoning: When AE Design requires proximity surveys to document customer facilities maintain required clearances from AE primary voltage facilities, this survey must be submitted per UCM § 1.10.3. Given the presence of transmission lines and the multiple clearance requirements documented on Sheet 3, AE Design may have required such a survey. The absence of this survey prevents verification of clearance compliance.

findings.comment: Provide documentation that Austin Energy removed the existing electric meter and service drop from the demolished facility before demolition. If not yet removed, submit work request to AE and document the removal per UCM § 1.10.13.
applicableAreas: Demolition of existing facility with electric service
findings.observation: Project involves demolition (facility demolished June 2022 per facts.md). Existing facility was an assisted living center that required electric service, meter, and service drop. No documentation found on current site plan or in supplementary documents confirming: (1) Austin Energy removed the electric meter and service drop before/during demolition, (2) whether site plan sheets include coordination notes for AE removal, or (3) evidence that work request was submitted to AE for removal. Sheet 8 (Demolition Plan) does not clearly document this coordination.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.13 requires that 'Existing electric service, meter, and service drop not coordinated with AE for removal before demolition may proceed.' The regulation requires: (1) written verification that utilities are suitable/sufficient (if continuing), and (2) after demolition approval but before demolition, contact AE to arrange removal. While demolition is already complete (June 2022), the current site plan submittal should document that this coordination occurred. The absence of clear documentation is a deficiency.
